punchline: A DNA test cleared a man who had spent fifteen years in prison, and the district attorney said he trusted his detective and a tape.
thirty_sec: A district attorney in Pennsylvania refused to accept a DNA result that cleared a man who had served fifteen years. Asked for his scientific basis, he said he had none, but he trusted his detective and the recorded confession. Tavris and Aronson do not call him a liar. For someone who sees himself as decent, doubting the lab is easier to live with than admitting he helped convict an innocent man.
